book.title: The Telegraph All New Cryptic Crosswords 4

clue.text: A fairy has endless row after drink

indicators.note: after places the quarrel following the fairy, in reading order

parts.note: taken as written
a peri is a fairy or sprite in Persian legend, a crossword favourite

indicators.note: endless says the word for row loses its final letter

parts.note: a tiff is a petty quarrel or row

explanation.surface: A fairy, having had a quarrel that goes on forever, then reaches for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal to sharpen the appetite.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for dress is read from bottom to top

parts.note: garb is clothing, dress

explanation.surface: Someone puts on fancy clothes and flaunts them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress up' reads as one phrase meaning put on finery; here 'up' turns the clothing word around.
explanation.definitionFit: To brag is to boast, which is a verbal way of showing off.

clue.text: Sensitive therapy ends stifling shout of pain

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, so the outer letters wrap around the cry
ends asks for just the first and last letters of therapy

parts.note: the outside pair of letters of this word, its start and finish, wrap the cry
ouch is the exclamation of sudden pain

explanation.surface: A delicate treatment that finishes by muffling a patient's yelp.
explanation.definitionFit: A touchy person is easily upset or offended, that is, oversensitive.

clue.text: Party leader, the French, a positive delight

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: only the opening letter of this word is used, as its leader
le is French for the
taken as written
to be positive is to be sure

explanation.surface: A French party leader proves to be a confident joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party leader' suggests a politician; it only asks for the first letter of Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasure is enjoyment or happiness, the same thing as delight.

clue.text: Tuna roll or a nut, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: read as food, a fish sandwich or a snack; read letter by letter, the phrase is the same forwards and backwards
perhaps marks the phrase as one example of the kind of thing wanted

explanation.walkthrough: The surface offers a choice of snacks; spelt out, 'tunarolloranut' reads the same in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A word or phrase that reads the same backwards as forwards is given this name, from Greek for running back again.

parts.note: re means on the subject of, about
alms are gifts of money to the poor

explanation.surface: Someone declares their view about welfare payments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'States' looks like a verb meaning declares; it is the noun, kingdoms.
explanation.definitionFit: Realms are kingdoms or countries, so states in the political sense.

indicators.note: on here just places the prompt beside the debts, one piece following straight after the other

parts.note: to spur is to urge on or prompt
IOUs are written promises to pay, so debts

explanation.surface: Someone sees through a fake who is pushing for money owed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spurious is false or counterfeit, a close synonym of phoney.

indicators.note: in puts the doctor inside the word for an infection

parts.note: a sore is an infected or inflamed spot on the skin
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A patient's infection keeps the doctor in the dark about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sombre means gloomy and shadowy, a synonym for dark in colour or mood.

indicators.note: the metal holds the iron within it, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: lead is a metal
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A metal with iron in it went green, as copper or rusting alloys discolour.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests corrosion; the question mark warns that the green is foliage instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree that has leafed has put out its leaves, so in spring it has turned green.

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the four words before it, read in order

parts.note: only the opening letter of this word is used
only the opening letter of this word is used
only the opening letter of this word is used
only the opening letter of this word is used

explanation.surface: A pharmacist's note on how a remedy is normally handed out at the start of a course.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer and also supplies its letters, so it is an all-in-one clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug is a medicine, a remedy dispensed by a pharmacist on prescription.

clue.text: Lamb with poetic bent in tune

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Charles Lamb, the essayist, had a poetic leaning and a sense of harmony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lamb with poetic bent' reads as a description of the writer; 'bent' is really the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are in tune get along in harmony, which is what compatible means.

indicators.note: the hovel takes in the tear, holding it inside itself

parts.note: a sty is a pigsty, hence a filthy hovel
a rent is a tear or rip in cloth

explanation.surface: Someone shut out of a shack in exchange for the rent money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid for housing; here it is a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: Something barred is marked with bars or stripes, so stripy describes it.

clue.text: Part of dinner I get ready

indicators.note: ready here means prepared, made up anew, so the letters are put into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook prepares one element of the evening meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The book's text has lost the 'I' the letters need; the anagram uses DINNER, I and GET.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingredient is one component of a mixture or recipe, one part of the whole.

clue.text: Dodgy sort with nude, most buxom

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or not in good order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shady character with a naked figure who is the most well-endowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Buxom means plump and full-figured, so the most buxom is the plumpest or roundest.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to calculate or ... something out
second meaning: a person's physical shape

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests exercising at the gym; 'work out' is really the verb to calculate.
explanation.definitionFit: Figure is both a verb meaning calculate and a noun for the shape of a human frame.

clue.text: Comeback from one with press release

indicators.note: to release is to set free, so these letters are set loose and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A statement from someone with a press release responding to criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press release' reads as a news statement; 'release' is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A comeback is a reply or retort, so a response.

clue.text: Place in the Azores or Tenerife

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of the first island's name and the little word after it

explanation.surface: Suggesting a location somewhere among the Atlantic holiday islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests choosing a destination; the letters span 'Azores' and 'or'.
explanation.definitionFit: A resort is a holiday destination, a place people go to stay.

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the irritable word goes round the artist and very

parts.note: testy means irritable, cross
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist is furious about a mocking portrait of himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very cross' looks like one phrase; 'very' goes with the artist inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque or absurd imitation, a caricature.

indicators.note: the dish holds the letter inside it

parts.note: a plate is a dish

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: only the opening letter of the vegetable is used, as its head

explanation.surface: Try a plate with an asparagus tip on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Asparagus head' reads as the vegetable's tip; here it is just the initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A palate is a sense of taste, especially a refined one for food and wine.

indicators.note: to wreck something is to smash it up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A submarine survives a disaster at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Here submarine is the adjective meaning beneath the sea surface, not the vessel.

clue.text: Youth from prison on a getaway

indicators.note: from means the answer is taken out of the run of words that follows

parts.note: the answer runs from the last letter of prison through on and a into the start of getaway

explanation.surface: A young offender escaping from jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonage is the legal state of being under age, hence youth or minority.

parts.note: to discover something is to see it
taken as written
W is the abbreviation for wife; the 's ties the wordplay to the definition

explanation.surface: Someone finds a toy belonging to his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive, but it only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A seesaw is a playground toy, a balanced plank that children ride up and down.

clue.text: Detective's hard on tart taking Ecstasy

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed below, so the hard letter comes last
taking means the word for tart takes in the drug letter

parts.note: slut is a slangy insult for a promiscuous woman, as is tart
E is the street name for the drug Ecstasy
H is the pencil-lead grade for hard

explanation.surface: A police officer is tough on a woman found with drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleuth is an investigator, a detective, originally a sleuth-hound tracking a scent.

indicators.note: fresh suggests something made anew, so these letters are arranged anew

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Letting fresh air in brings someone round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh air' reads as one phrase; 'Fresh' is the instruction and 'air' joins the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To invigorate is to give new energy and strength, which is what reviving someone does.

indicators.note: by means next to, so the expected word stands beside the letter for left

parts.note: something due is expected, as a train is due

explanation.surface: A showdown that was foreseen by the political left.
explanation.definitionFit: A duel is a formal fight between two opponents, a direct confrontation.

indicators.note: embracing means hugging, so the character's name holds the letter for right

parts.note: Desperate Dan is the hugely strong cowboy in the British children's comic The Dandy

explanation.surface: A frantic person clutching a right-hand turn as things blossom.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a character in the British comic The Dandy. 'Blooming' is a mild British swear word, not flowering.
explanation.definitionFit: Darn is a polite euphemism for damn, an exclamation with the same mild force as blooming.

parts.note: taken as written
the Gents is the British term for a men's public lavatory

explanation.surface: A lavatory used as a meeting place by spies, a classic Cold War dead drop.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gents is the everyday British name for a men's public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Agents are people working secretly for a government, as spies do.

clue.text: Case of rosé in fullness and body

indicators.note: in places the case of the wine inside the word for body

parts.note: an entity is a body or thing with its own existence

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: the case of the word is its outer pair of letters, the first and the last

explanation.surface: A wine tasting note praising the fullness and body of a rosé.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fullness and body' reads like wine-tasting jargon; 'body' is wordplay and 'fullness' alone defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Entirety is the state of being whole and complete, the same as fullness.
